messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testEscapedQuote_LANG_477` uses ExtendedMessageFormat with a pattern containing escaped single quotes (`it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!`). According to the current bug report, ExtendedMessageFormat experiences an OutOfMemoryError with custom format registries when patterns contain single quotes.

Looking at the ExtendedMessageFormat constructor used by the test:
- `ExtendedMessageFormat(String pattern, Map registry)` delegates to `ExtendedMessageFormat(String pattern, Locale locale, Map registry)`.
- This constructor sets the locale, assigns the custom registry to the instance, and calls `applyPattern(pattern)`.

The `applyPattern(String pattern)` method:
- If no custom registry, uses the superclass MessageFormat's pattern application.
- If a custom registry is present, it parses the pattern manually.
- It processes the pattern char by char, handling quoted strings (`case QUOTE`) by calling `appendQuotedString`.
- It also handles format elements and attempts to recognize and replace custom formats from the registry.

The `appendQuotedString` method:
- Processes quoted strings starting at the QUOTE character.
- It manages escaped quotes (`''`) by appending a single quote and moving the parse position forward.
- It throws an IllegalArgumentException if the quoted string is unterminated.

Given the symptoms of OutOfMemory and the failing test pattern which has doubled single quotes and normal quoted substrings, the problem likely arises in the parsing of quoted strings inside `applyPattern`.

Specifically, the while loop processes each character and delegates quotes to `appendQuotedString`, which tries to handle escaped quotes. This logic probably does not handle all edge cases correctly when a custom registry is involved: it may fail to advance parse position properly or fail to break out of loops when processing complex patterns with escaped quotes, leading to infinite loops or excessive parsing causing the OutOfMemoryError.

The root cause is a bug in the handling of single quotes and escaped quotes in the pattern parsing logic inside `applyPattern` combined with `appendQuotedString` when a custom format registry is used. This leads to runaway parsing behavior and memory exhaustion.

The recent bug reports are unrelated and do not mention ExtendedMessageFormat or similar pattern parsing or escaping issues, so they are not relevant.

Hence, the OutOfMemoryError originates from flawed single quote parsing and quote escaping in ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern and appendQuotedString when custom registries are used.

Next, I will indicate the best methods to fix this issue.
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.appendQuotedString(java.lang.String, java.text.ParsePosition, java.lang.StringBuffer, boolean)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
